subject: Request: delegated network attribution for Private deployment - HelixGrid
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@helixgrid.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: HelixGrid Network Ops <netops@helixgrid.com>
Date: 2028-04-02T15:12:00Z
Subject: Request: delegated network attribution for Private deployment - HelixGrid

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. As we discussed, HelixGrid will be running the customer edge and peering for the Private deployment in our colo. Our ops team expects the vast majority of tail latency we see to be driven by our transit and edge routers, not Redwood's inference runtime.

To move the contract forward we need to propose an SLA appendix (or carve-out) that:
- Excludes customer-managed edge/peering transit from Redwood's 99.9% P95 latency SLO for Private deployments when traffic egresses/ingresses through HelixGrid-provisioned routers.
- Defines the evidence HelixGrid must provide to support attribution (e.g., NetFlow exports, traceroute captures, sFlow, router syslog snippets).
- Specifies an operational escalation path and a short review cadence after go-live (30 days).

Can Redwood provide a suggested appendix language we can redline? Also helpful: an example list of monitoring/format expectations and minimum retention windows for logs so our security team can confirm compliance. I've attached a high-level network diagram to show where we control the handoff.

Thanks,
Alex Turner
Network Engineering
HelixGrid
Attachment: helixgrid-network-diagram.pdf
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@helixgrid.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-03T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: delegated network attribution for Private deployment - HelixGrid

Alex — thanks for the clear note and the diagram. Attaching a draft SLA appendix (proposed-sla-appendix-draft.docx) that sketches the carve-out language and the evidence we typically accept. High-level summary of the proposal: 

- Attribution carve-out: When customer-managed edge/peering is the proximate cause of end-to-end latency (as demonstrated by mutually agreed evidence), Redwood will not count those incidents toward the Private deployment latency SLO.

- Evidence & formats: NetFlow or sFlow exports (48 hours of raw samples), time-stamped traceroute packet captures spanning the incident window, and router syslog entries with timestamped interface counters. Specific field requirements are in the appendix draft.

- Measurement & tooling: Redwood will provide a weekly latency evidence report for the customer to review. If both parties agree that network transit is causal, the incident is excluded. Disputes escalate to an ops review within 3 business days.

- Operational controls: a 30-day post-go-live review, and a required baseline capture (48h) before we flip production traffic.

Next steps I propose:
1) HelixGrid redlines the draft appendix and returns with the network diagram and sample NetFlow export (anonymized) — your security team can scrub IPs.
2) Our infra team (cc'd: Karthik & Vanessa) reviews the format and adds any collection/retention constraints.
3) Legal folds final wording into the Master Services Agreement and we lock a DocuSign wrapper.

I'm available for a 30-minute ops-level call Friday if you want to walk through the evidence formats.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed-sla-appendix-draft.docx

Date: 2028-04-04T09:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: delegated network attribution for Private deployment - HelixGrid

FWIW — quick infra/legal ops note from my side after skimming the draft:

- Wording: Replace generic 'attribution' phrasing with an objective filter: "If packet-level traceroutes and NetFlow indicate >85% of queuing delay occurring on customer-controlled interfaces for the incident window, the incident will be attributed to customer-managed network transit." This avoids open-ended disputes.

- Evidence retention: Recommend minimum 30 days retention for flow samples and 365 days for aggregated latency summaries. We should be explicit about time sync requirements (NTP-synced timestamps, required timezone/offset format).

- Monitoring: Add a requirement that HelixGrid provide at least one sample TCP traceroute (MTR) per week for the first 60 days post cutover to establish baseline, then monthly thereafter.

- Grace window: For the first 14 days after production traffic begins, incidents will be case-by-case and excluded from SLA triggers to account for routing convergence.

I've attached a redline text with suggested language edits (sla-appendix-redline.txt). Happy to join the ops call Friday to walk through specifics.

—Karthik
Head of Infrastructure Partnerships, Redwood Inference
Attachment: sla-appendix-redline.txt
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@helixgrid.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: HelixGrid Network Ops <netops@helixgrid.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-05T16:43:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: delegated network attribution for Private deployment - HelixGrid

Mina / team — thanks for the rapid turnaround and the clear list of asks. HelixGrid can sign up to the proposed approach in principle. A few clarifications before we redline: 

1) Retention: we can provide 30 days for raw NetFlow exports; aggregated summaries for 12 months is fine.
2) Traceroute cadence: weekly MTRs for 60 days works. We'll provide an initial 48h baseline capture as requested.
3) Time sync: we use GPS-synced NTP; we'll include timezone offsets in all exports.
4) Third-party audit: we accept monthly evidence-driven exclusion but we'd like a clause that allows either party to request a neutral third-party review if attribution remains disputed after ops escalation.

I've attached our sanitized network diagram and a sample anonymized NetFlow extract to demonstrate format (we'll share a live sample over SFTP for the ops review). Can Redwood confirm the format you prefer for NetFlow (v5 vs v9) and any preferred CSV column ordering for faster ingestion?

If that matches your asks, we'll send a redline of the draft appendix and we can aim to get legal signoff in the next 7–10 business days.

Thanks,
Alex Turner
Network Engineering
HelixGrid
Attachments: helixgrid-network-diagram.pdf (sanitized), sample-netflow-anon.csv
